comment: Hand-written roasts for a day's lowest scores. Add one object to days when the group writes them. A day with no entry shows nothing on the board. Do not generate roast text in the page.

roasts.text: Ben said he rocked it. The rock was a 42 in Hamilton, New Zealand, with the sad face on. Paris was a 98. The other four pins were a tour of places he has decided do not count. Semey closed him at 68. Last place, and the quote is doing more damage than the score.

Peter bullseyed Paris and then smiled through a 68 in Semey, Kazakhstan. That smile is not confidence. That is a man from small-group Alabama finding the milk suspicious and pinning the steppe anyway. Fifth place, eight behind Sam, and the 100 does not travel.

Sam seconded the meh and then put a confused 66 on Semey to prove it. Hamilton was a 98. Kazakhstan was the whole personality. He finished three points behind Micah, who also said meh and at least got to 70 on the last pin. Seconding a meh is not a strategy.

Ben said he does well in the countries that matter, then shot a 98 in Mobile, Alabama and a 59 in both Maracaibo and Pucallpa. Venezuela and Peru have apparently been removed from the list of countries. Last place, again, and the neutral face on Maracaibo was doing a lot of work.

Yesterday's winner clapped for himself twice. An 80 in Maracaibo and an 80 in Pucallpa, both with the applause emoji, is not a victory lap. Nuremberg was a 95. The rest of the route was Casey negotiating with the jungle. Fifth place, 114 off his own Monday.

Andy put a perfect 100 on Mobile and still finished in the roast corner. The sparkle on Pucallpa was an 80. Peter beat him by 5. Sam beat him by 9. A bullseye in Alabama does not cover a bedtime story in Peru.

Last place on a day the winner shot 973. Ben flushed a 66 on Tel Aviv, smiled through a 71 in Miaoli, and sparkled an 80 in Dijon like the mustard was the hard part. Fort Knox was the only place he recognized, because it has gold in the name. Then Bukavu handed him a 56 and a grimace. The doctor was in the Congo. Ben was not.

Peter went 97, 95, 97 around a 60 in Miaoli City and called it a day. That 60 is not a near miss. That is looking at Taiwan, thinking about Alabama, and planting the pin in the wrong ocean. He closed Bukavu at 75 with the crying-laugh emoji, which is the correct reaction to finishing fifth.

Sam dropped a perfect 100 on Miaoli and still landed in the roast corner. The star on Bukavu was for an 82. An 82, with a gold star, on the last pin, is how you turn a Human GPS into fourth place. Casey beat him by 48 and never left the fire emoji. The leopard cat rice was not the problem, Sam.

Opened strong with a 93, then spent round 3 on the wrong continent because of 'kids', and said rounds 4 and 5 were places he 'didn't know existed.' He scored a 1 on Tonga. One. The kids are not the problem, Ben.

Missed Nukuʻalofa by 18,000 km and then looked up that half the Earth's circumference is 20,000 km, as if that helped his case. That's not a miss, that's a round trip. Scored a perfect 0 on the final round.
After a 53 in Lesotho and a 43 in Tonga, Peter told the group he 'felt violated.' Peter, the map didn't do anything to you. You did this to yourself.
